## Appearance

Gilbert is a tall, handsome fellow with broad shoulders, curly brown hair, and roguish hazel eyes that are clear and straightforward. He is characterized by a frank face and a mouth often twisted into a teasing smile. At one point, he appears noticeably pale and thin.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 ch.Lady P58](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0058), [v3 ch.Weddings P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022)_

## Personality

A clever, determined, and good-natured individual, he possesses a strong sense of humor along with a well-known stubbornness. Naturally popular and known for his teasing demeanor, he approaches life with ambition, zest, and a determination to get the best out of life while putting the best back into it. Academically and professionally driven, he aims for High Honors and the [Cooper](../character/cooper.md) Prize, while pursuing a career as a doctor to fight disease, pain, and ignorance through honest work. His practical ambitions also extend to purchasing the [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) place.

## History

Gilbert Blythe grows up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) after spending three years in Alberta for his father's health. Returning to school, he attempts to make peace with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) after pulling her hair, but she smashes a slate over his head and refuses to speak to him for years. Despite her stony silence, Gilbert enters an intense academic rivalry with her, ultimately tying with her for first place on the [Island](../codex/places.md#island) on the Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) entrance examinations. After completing their studies at Queen's, Gilbert wins the class medal, but he selflessly surrenders his appointed teaching position in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) so [Anne](../character/anne.md) can stay near [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). This generous act leads to their long-awaited reconciliation, and the two become close friends while working together to found the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society). As they grow older and attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) together, Gilbert's feelings turn romantic, but [Anne](../character/anne.md) rejects his initial marriage proposal, leaving him heartbroken. Distancing himself, he is briefly rumored to be involved with [Christine Stuart](../character/christine-stuart.md), but after surviving a life-threatening battle with typhoid fever, he proposes to [Anne](../character/anne.md) a second time and earns her eager acceptance. Following their wedding in the [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) orchard, Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne.md) move to [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor), where he begins his medical practice and they bond with local neighbors like Captain Jim and [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md). After enduring the tragic loss of their firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne.md) later welcome a healthy son named [James Matthew](../character/james-a.md). Following Captain Jim's peaceful death, Gilbert proposes purchasing the larger [Morgan](../character/morgan.md) place in [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary to accommodate their expanding family and medical practice. Settled in their new home at [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), Gilbert continues his career as a dedicated local physician, attending to the community and reviving young [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) when she faints during a church service.

## Quotes

> "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

> "You’re just tired, Anne. Come, forget it all and take a walk with me—a ramble back through the woods beyond the marsh. There should be something there I want to show you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Autumn P15](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0015)

> "No. I only know it should be, from something I saw there in spring. Come on. We’ll pretend we are two children again and we’ll go the way of the wind."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Autumn P17](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0017)

> "Here’s a fallen tree with a cushion of moss. Sit down, Anne—it will serve for a woodland throne. I’ll climb for some apples. They all grow high—the tree had to reach up to the sunlight."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Autumn P34](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0034)

> "I persist in dreaming it, although it has often seemed to me that it could never come true. I dream of a home with a hearth-fire in it, a cat and dog, the footsteps of friends—and you!"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v3 ch.Time P22](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0022)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne.md) began as academic rivals, a dynamic ignited when Gilbert teased her by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' prompting [Anne](../character/anne.md) to smash a slate over his head and hold a long grudge. Over time, their intense competition transformed into a close friendship and comradeship as they attended [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) together. They eventually entered into a romantic relationship and were married.
